clue.text: Standing out for what could be potato worker?

blocks.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
a potato is an example of a tuber
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A comic riddle about a labourer who sticks out from the crowd, perhaps toiling in a potato field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' flags that potato is only one example of a tuber, so the wordplay reads as 'for tuber worker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something protuberant bulges or sticks outward from its surroundings, the literal sense of standing out.

clue.text: Coup when school has placed first

indicators.note: 'first' places the item just named at the front of the answer, ahead of the other

blocks.note: to place something is to put it
SCH is a standard abbreviation for school

explanation.walkthrough: The word order is school then placed, but 'has placed first' puts the placing word ahead of the school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden, violent attempt to seize government power, the German word for a coup d'etat.

clue.text: Remark on job where one’s always on the lookout

definitions.text: where one’s always on the lookout

a job or position is a post

explanation.surface: Someone passes comment about a job that requires constant vigilance.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are plain synonyms; the only trick is that 'on' in a down clue means the first piece stacks above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a military position from which soldiers keep watch over enemy movements.

clue.text: Steadiness of university supporting dreaming Walter losing heart

explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' looks like a positional instruction for a down clue, but here it is simply FOR. MITTY loses its central T to give MITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformity is sameness and consistency without variation, which is what steadiness describes.

clue.text: Flat like number ten, but not thirteen

definitions.text: like number ten, but not thirteen

blocks.note: first meaning: level, smooth

blocks.clueFragment: like number ten, but not thirteen
blocks.note: second meaning: divisible by two, as ten is and thirteen is not

explanation.walkthrough: 'number ten' tempts a solver toward Downing Street; it is just the integer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a level surface and also integers exactly divisible by two, which ten is and thirteen is not.

clue.text: Thorough idiot — I work for two — useless

taken as written
a piece of music for two performers is a duo

explanation.walkthrough: US for useless (from 'unserviceable') is a convention worth learning; 'work for two' is a musical work, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An assiduous person shows great care and perseverance, attending to every detail of a task.

clue.text: Film appearing on surface like a mountain lake, perhaps

clue.text: Second of gumboots in template cobbled next to last

blocks.note: the second letter of gumboots
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: One with stamina in exercises beginning on ropes and one who will face walls

the first letter of ropes

clue.text: Nymph upsetting Diana

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Did badly in what thespians did, taking a lot of hits?

clue.text: Snake is a hoax when there’s nothing around

blocks.note: taken as written
tax is income collected by government

explanation.surface: A complaint that a perpetual shortfall in tax income is hitting the public treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a treasure chest to go with the revenue; it is the anatomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the anatomical part of the body between neck and abdomen, the ribcage area.

clue.text: Attempt cricketers mounted

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going upward, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: batsmen in cricket are called bats

explanation.surface: A cricket team tries climbing onto horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: BATS for batsmen is cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make a try, so a stab is an informal word for an attempt.

clue.text: Returning bad old fruit

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: bad is evil
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Sending back fruit that has gone off with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad old fruit' reads as rotten produce; it is the wordplay plus the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the olive is a small stone fruit, the drupe of the olive tree.

clue.text: Love like an old PM? Not that!

indicators.note: 'not that' says to leave out the word named, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: Margaret Thatcher was a British prime minister
the suffix -ish means 'like'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should love like a former prime minister, then recoils at the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not that!' sounds like an exclamation of horror; it tells you to remove 'that' from the PM's name, leaving the end of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to hold them dear and protect them, a synonym for love as a verb.

clue.text: Mostly keen about new journey round in train

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
about means surrounding, so one piece encloses the others

blocks.note: keen means eager
N is the abbreviation for new
a tour is a round trip

explanation.surface: An eager traveller embarks on a fresh round trip by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train; it is a retinue of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of followers or attendants is a retinue, and an entourage is the group accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Care for dog that’s eaten rook — pointer, perhaps?

indicators.note: what has been eaten has gone inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: to care for is to tend
a setter is a gundog breed
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: Looking after a gundog that has swallowed a bird; a pointer is a dog too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointer' wants to be another gundog alongside the setter; with the question mark it is someone who points the way for others to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter shows others the direction fashion will take, a pointer in the sense of a guide or indicator.

clue.text: In hollow, I’m sheltering antelope that shows injury

indicators.note: one item in another is placed inside it
to shelter something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a dent is a hollow
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
the sable is an African antelope

explanation.surface: Someone hiding in a ditch with a wounded antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Two enclosures nest: the small word goes inside the hollow, then the antelope goes inside that small word.
explanation.definitionFit: Disablement is a state of physical incapacity, typically caused by a wound or harm to the body.
